explanation: Treat path components as a stack. Ignore dots and empty components; a parent component cancels a normal preceding component. Preserve unresolved parents only for relative paths. Prepend a slash only for absolute paths.
timeComplexity: O(n), where n is path length Every component is classified once, pushed at most once and popped at most once; joining emits the result once.
spaceComplexity: O(n) Split components and the surviving component stack together require linear storage.
attribution: Original Python implementation authored for EPI Practice from its displayed contract and independently authored C# solution; no upstream reference source adapted.
correctness: The component stack always represents the normalized processed prefix. A name appends one level, a dot changes nothing, and a parent removes a normal level if possible. Only unresolved relative parents are retained, so the final joined components describe the same rooted or relative path.
walkthrough: For oak/./elm/../ash, ignore the dot, append elm, then cancel elm on the parent step. Append ash and join to obtain oak/ash.
edgeCases: Repeated slashes do not create components.
A fully cancelled relative path becomes empty.
Unresolved leading parents are preserved for relative paths.
